literal: Hostility, they say, is to all living beings the disease that brings about the lack of good character called division.
translation: Hostility, they say, is a disease for all living beings that breeds the ill disposition of division.
modern: இகல் என்று சொல்லப்படுவது, எல்லா உயிர்களுக்கும் பிரிவினை என்னும் தீய குணத்தை உண்டாக்குகின்ற ஒரு நோயாகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines hostility (ikal) as a harmful disease (noy) that affects all living beings. It explains that hostility is the root cause of 'division' (pakal), which is described here as a complete lack of good character (panpinmai). Instead of bringing people together, hostility infects minds and creates separation, destroying the natural harmony of relationships. By comparing hostility to a disease, the poet emphasizes its destructive and infectious nature.
